*adjusts monocle and sighs with the weariness of a man whose yacht crew once served Château Margaux at room temperature*

Good heavens, Lovey, come look at this! Someone from the *working class* has submitted code that handles actual money. I haven't seen such financial recklessness since Gilligan tried to start a coconut-based cryptocurrency.

**CRITICAL ISSUES (The kind that would make the Howells lose their fortune)**

**SQL Injection - Lines 97, 105, 117, 138, 145, 183, 190, 211** — My word! String concatenation directly into SQL queries. Any vagrant with a keyboard could execute `?id=1; DROP TABLE orders--` and obliterate your data faster than a monsoon capsizes a Minnow.

**Storing Credit Cards in Plaintext - Lines 28, 82** — You're storing *credit cards* in your database?! Even the most nouveau riche understands PCI-DSS compliance! This is a violation that carries fines heavier than my gold bullion collection.

**HIGH SEVERITY (Behavior unbecoming of proper society)**

**No Authentication/Authorization** — Lines 40, 92, 127, 148 — *Anyone* can cancel *anyone's* order? View *anyone's* data? This is like letting the castaways into my private wine cellar!

**Race Conditions - Lines 69-75, 143-149** — Goroutines firing inventory reservations without waiting? If they fail after payment succeeds, you've charged customers for products you can't deliver. *Frightfully* poor form.

**Loop Variable Capture - Lines 143-149** — The goroutine captures `productID` and `quantity` by reference. Classic Go blunder. Every iteration will use the *last* values. My Harvard professors would be appalled.

**Ignored Errors - Lines 43, 54, 60, 63, 65, 72, 107, 161, 187** — Discarding errors like yesterday's caviar! Payment failures, inventory checks, database operations—all silently ignored while you merrily proceed.

**MEDIUM SEVERITY (Social faux pas)**

**Float64 for Currency - Line 24** — Using floating-point for *money*? `0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3` in IEEE 754, you poor dear. Use integers representing cents or a decimal library.

**Unbounded Cache - Line 90** — No eviction policy? This cache will consume memory until your server collapses like the Professor's radio experiments.

**No Timeouts on HTTP Calls - Lines 49, 61, 134** — External services could hang indefinitely, blocking your goroutines forever.

**Response Body Leaks - Lines 54, 63, 134, 161, 186** — Never closing `resp.Body`. Memory leaks are *so* déclassé.

**Cache Without Mutex - Line 90** — You lock for nothing but write to the cache *outside* the mutex. Data races, my good man!

**LOW SEVERITY (Matters for the help to address)**

**No Request Timeouts/Contexts - Line 40** — Accept a context, use it. Lines 180-182 show `context` imported but never used.

**Credit Card in Export - Lines 216-217** — Even masked, you're exposing card data in CSV exports. The auditors will have *conniptions*.

*sets down brandy snifter*

"Works in staging," you say? My boy, the Titanic *worked* in staging too. This code needs a complete rewrite before it touches a single dollar of *anyone's* money—even the Skipper's.

**REJECTED.** Do come back when you've hired proper developers.
